topic: Literary Awards (Jnanpith, Booker, Saraswati, Vyas Samman)
description: This topic covers the most prestigious national and international literary awards. It is highly crucial for the Static GK section of competitive exams, focusing on the founders, first winners, and specific criteria for each award.

sections.title: Jnanpith Award
sections.description: The highest and oldest literary honor in India, awarded annually for outstanding contribution to literature.

historical_events.significance: Instituted by the Bharatiya Jnanpith Trust, which was founded by the Sahu Shanti Prasad Jain family.
Awarded to the eminent Malayalam poet G. Sankara Kurup for his poetry collection 'Odakkuzhal' (The Bamboo Flute).

key_associations.extra_info: Honoured for her prominent Bengali novel 'Pratham Pratishruti' (The First Promise).
Awarded for his outstanding overall lifetime contribution to English literature.

important_facts.fact: The award is bestowed only upon Indian citizens for writing in English or any of the 22 languages included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
The Jnanpith Award comprises a cash prize of Rs. 11 lakh, a citation, and a bronze replica of Vagdevi (the Hindu Goddess of Learning, Saraswati).

sections.title: The Booker and International Booker Prizes
sections.description: The most prestigious and widely recognized international awards in the field of literature.

key_concepts.explanation: A literary prize awarded each year for the best original novel written in the English language and published in the United Kingdom or Ireland.
An international literary award hosted in the UK, given for a single book that has been translated into English and published in the UK or Ireland.

key_associations.item: First Indian Citizen to win the Booker Prize
key_associations.extra_info: She won the prestigious award for her acclaimed debut novel 'The God of Small Things'.

key_associations.item: First Hindi Novel to win the International Booker
key_associations.extra_info: Authored by Geetanjali Shree and translated into English by Daisy Rockwell.

key_associations.associated_with: Salman Rushdie, Kiran Desai, Aravind Adiga
key_associations.extra_info: Rushdie won in 1981 for 'Midnight's Children', Desai in 2006 for 'The Inheritance of Loss', and Adiga in 2008 for 'The White Tiger'.

sections.title: Saraswati Samman
sections.description: One of the most reputed literary awards in India, recognizing excellence in prose and poetry.

historical_events.significance: Instituted by the K.K. Birla Foundation to recognize outstanding literary works by Indian citizens.

key_associations.extra_info: He was awarded for his monumental four-volume autobiography (including 'Kya Bhooloon Kya Yaad Karoon' and 'Dashdwar Se Sopan Tak').

important_facts.fact: It is given annually for an outstanding prose or poetry work published in the last 10 years in any of the 22 languages of the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.

sections.title: Vyas Samman
sections.description: A prestigious literary award presented by the K.K. Birla Foundation, dedicated exclusively to the Hindi language.

historical_events.significance: Established alongside the Saraswati Samman by the K.K. Birla Foundation, but with a strict focus on Hindi literature.

key_associations.extra_info: Awarded for his critical and historical work 'Bharat ke Pracheen Bhasha Parivar aur Hindi' (India's ancient language families and Hindi).

important_facts.fact: The Vyas Samman is awarded annually exclusively for an outstanding Hindi literary work authored by an Indian citizen and published during the past 10 years.

sections.title: Sahitya Akademi & Other Notable Awards
sections.description: Other significant literary awards relevant for Static GK and key facts related to the Nobel Prize in Literature.

key_associations.extra_info: Presented annually for literary works that deeply emphasize Indian philosophy and culture.
Awarded exclusively to authors belonging to Rajasthan for their outstanding literary work in Hindi or Rajasthani.

important_facts.fact: The Sahitya Akademi Award, established in 1954, is conferred in 24 languages (the 22 Eighth Schedule languages, plus English and Rajasthani).
Rabindranath Tagore was the first Asian to win the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913, honoured for his deeply sensitive, fresh and beautiful collection of poetry, 'Gitanjali'.
